chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the saying of the Exalted:
Verily, Allah enjoins justice and benevolence,
Justice is equidistribution (fairness), and benevolence is favor (generosity).

key_terms.الْإِحْسَانُ: Benevolence; doing good beyond what is required
key_terms.الْإِنْصَافُ: Equidistribution; treating equally or giving one's due
key_terms.الْعَدْلُ: Justice; fairness and giving due rights

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between justice and benevolence in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) provides a precise jurisprudential distinction between 'adl' (justice) as fulfilling obligatory rights (insaf) and 'ihsan' (benevolence) as voluntary supererogatory generosity (tafaddul). This definition establishes a foundational framework in Shia ethics, distinguishing between the minimum requirement of fairness and the higher spiritual ideal of grace. Such clarity aids in understanding the gradation of moral duties in Islamic law and spirituality.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 231. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said about Allāh’s saying:
Verily, Allāh enjoins justice (‘adl) and benevolence (iḥsān),(Qur’ān,16:90).
Here ‘adl means equidistribution and iḥsān means favour.
